title: Relative ampleness on a scheme base change of an algebraic-space line module
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], let $f:X\to T$, and let $L$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module on its small etale site (in particular, $L$ may be a line module). For a $T$-scheme $B\to T$, regard $B$ and $T$ as algebraic spaces through their representable sheaves [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space] and form the actual sheaf fibre product $Z=X\times_TB$ and its projection $q:Z\to X$ [def-sfb-space-sheaf-fibre-product]. Pull $L$ back by the canonical ringed-etale tensor functor $q^*$ [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Define the relative ample scheme-test condition for $(f,L,B)$ to mean that there exists an etale scheme object $U\to Z$ which is an isomorphism of represented sheaves, and, for every affine open $W\subset B$, the restriction to $p^{-1}(W)$ of the ordinary module corresponding to $q^*L$ is invertible and ample [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], where $p:U\to B$ is the canonical fibre-product projection. The ordinary module is restriction to Zariski opens [def-trf-space-module-scheme-restriction]; restriction along the open inclusion is ordinary tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Thus the condition includes that $Z$ itself is a scheme, not just that $Z$ admits a scheme atlas.
